text: From Granite Falls, follow the Mountain Loop Highway east about 31 miles to Barlow Pass, at about 2,360 ft, where the pavement ends, and park in the Barlow Pass lot. The gated gravel road to Monte Cristo leaves from here and is open only to foot and bike traffic. A Northwest Forest Pass or America the Beautiful pass is required to park.

From Granite Falls, drive the Mountain Loop Highway east past the Verlot Public Service Center and continue 19.3 miles beyond it to Barlow Pass, where the pavement ends, and park at the Barlow Pass Trailhead at about 2,360 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass or day fee is required to park.

From the Verlot Public Service Center follow the Mountain Loop Highway east about 19.5 miles to the large parking area at Barlow Pass. The highway is paved the whole way now, and the lot fills on summer weekends.
From US 101 west of Port Angeles, turn south onto Olympic Hot Springs Road and drive about 2 miles to the Madison Falls parking area, where the road is closed to vehicles.

From Port Angeles, drive about 8 miles west on US 101 and turn left onto Olympic Hot Springs Road just past the Elwha River bridge. Follow it about 2 miles to the Madison Falls parking area at the park boundary, where the road is closed to vehicles. An overnight wilderness permit is required.

The North Fork Sauk River Trailhead sits at about 2,050 ft off FR 49, the Sloan Creek Road, and it is where Trail #649 starts up the valley. A Northwest Forest Pass is required, and there is a kiosk at the trailhead. Do not plan on coming in from the west: the White Chuck River Road (FR 23) remains washed out, and this has been the primary approach to Glacier Peak since the White Chuck River Trail

From Darrington, drive the Mountain Loop Highway south about 16 miles and turn left (east) onto FS Road 49, the North Fork Sauk Road. Follow it about 6.4 miles to the North Fork Sauk Trailhead at the road end near 2,100 ft; the road is rough and a high-clearance vehicle helps. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park.

pins.name: North Fork Sauk Trailhead (FR-49, Sloan Creek Road)

text: From Darrington, drive the Mountain Loop Highway south about 16 miles to Forest Road 49 (Sloan Creek Road), turn east and drive about 6.4 miles to the North Fork Sauk Trailhead parking lot at the road end. A Northwest Forest Pass is required, and a free Glacier Peak Wilderness permit is self-issued at the trailhead.

text: From Granite Falls, drive the Mountain Loop Highway east about 26 mi (about 14.5 mi past the Verlot Public Service Center) to the Big Four Picnic Area and Ice Caves Trailhead, at about 1,640 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park.

pins.name: Bedal Creek / Bedal Basin Trailhead (end of FR 4096)

text: Drive the Mountain Loop Highway to Forest Road 4096 and follow that rough, narrow spur - a 4WD road about three miles long where high clearance genuinely helps - to its end at the Bedal Creek trailhead, around 2,790 feet.

From Granite Falls, follow the Mountain Loop Highway east about 10 miles to the Verlot Public Service Center. Continue about 1 mile, cross the South Fork Stillaguamish River, and turn right onto Mount Pilchuck Road, FS Road 42. Drive about 6.8 miles, mostly rough gravel with a paved final stretch, to the road-end trailhead at about 3,100 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass or America the Beautiful pass is

From US-2 at Coles Corner, take SR 207 north 4.3 miles and bear right onto Chiwawa Loop Road, then turn left onto the Chiwawa River Road (FR 62) and follow it about 23 miles, paved and then gravel, to the large Trinity lot just before the gate at the road end. The last stretch is rough and rutted; high clearance helps. A Northwest Forest Pass is required to park, and a free wilderness permit is se

Take the Mountain Loop Highway to FR 4096, about 18.25 miles south of Darrington and roughly a mile south of Bedal Campground. The spur is rough and narrow and runs about 3 miles to its end at the Bedal Creek Trailhead, around 2,790 ft, so bring high clearance or 4WD. Bedal Creek Trail #705 starts from the road end. This is the preferred trailhead for this side of Sloan because it avoids the river

Drive Chiwawa River Road (FR 6200) to its end at the old Trinity mine site. The road is rough and high clearance is worth having; it commonly stays snowbound until early summer, which sets the start of the season here more than conditions on the peak do. Carry water from home — there is none at the trailhead.

From US-2 at Coles Corner, take SR-207 north 4.2 miles past the Wenatchee River crossing and bear right onto Chiwawa Loop Road. After 1.3 miles turn left onto Chiwawa River Road (FS Road 62) and drive about 22 miles, the last 11 on rough gravel, keeping left at the final junction for the Trinity Trailhead at about 2,800 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass is required and a free wilderness permit is self-i

From US 2 at Coles Corner, take SR 207 north about 4 miles and bear right onto Chiwawa Loop Road, then after 1.3 miles turn left onto Chiwawa River Road (Forest Road 62). Follow it about 22 miles and keep left at the final junction to the Trinity Trailhead at about 2,800 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass and a free self-issued wilderness permit are needed. The road has been closed below the trailhead at

From Chiwawa River Road / FR 6200, turn onto FR 6211 (Phelps Creek Road) and follow it to the road-end lot. The trail leaving the lot is Phelps Creek Trail #1511, heading north up-valley through open forest — wide and nearly level, which is not what the rest of the day looks like.

Drive the Chiwawa River Road (FR 62) roughly twenty-two miles, then turn onto the Phelps Creek Road, FR 6211, and follow it to its end at the Phelps Creek Trailhead (about 3,500 ft), near Trinity in Chelan County.

Drive the Chiwawa River Road (FR-62) to the Phelps Creek Road spur, FR 6211, and follow it to its end at the Phelps Creek Trailhead (3,500 ft). The road typically opens with spring snowmelt by June. No Northwest Forest Pass is required here, but sign the self-issue register before starting up Phelps Creek Trail #1511.

From US-2 at Coles Corner take WA-207 north, then Chiwawa River Road (FR-62) about 22 miles — paved for the first eleven, gravel and rough after that — and finish with 2.3 miles up Phelps Creek Road (FR-6211) to the road end. Low-clearance vehicles struggle on the last stretch. Cloudy Pass can also be reached from Holden Village up Railroad Creek or from Trinity over Buck Creek Pass, but both are

Drive to the road end on Phelps Creek Road (FR 6211). Both the Northwest Forest Pass and the self-issue wilderness permit are handled at the trailhead kiosk. Note this is the Phelps Creek side: the Railroad Creek and Spider Gap approach out of Holden Village reaches the same basin from the east but is far longer, and is normally only used by parties already on the Lyman Lake loop.

pins.name: FR 4096 Pullout / Merry Brook Climbers' Path

text: Mountain Loop Highway to just past Bedal Campground, then up FR 4096 roughly 1.3 miles to near its second or third switchback (~2,100-2,200 ft). The pullout holds about five cars, and the start is marked only by a small cairn in the roadside grass about 100 ft up the bank — it is notoriously easy to drive past, so GPS-mark it on the way in.

From I-5 exit 208, drive east on SR-530 through Arlington to Darrington, about 28 miles, then turn right at the four-way stop in town onto the Mountain Loop Highway and follow it south roughly 14 miles — paved at first, then graveled — to FR-2095, the Mt. Pugh Spur Road, marked with a large sign on the left. Turn onto FR-2095, a narrow, one-lane, unpaved road, and continue about 1.5 miles to the t

pins.name: Mount Pugh Trailhead, FR 2095 second switchback

text: From I-5 exit 208, head east 4 miles on Highway 530 to Arlington, then continue east on SR 530 another 28 miles to Darrington. At the four-way intersection in town turn right onto the Mountain Loop Highway and follow it, paved and then graveled, for roughly 12.5 to 14 miles to a prominent Mount Pugh sign where FR 2095 branches off on the left. FR 2095 is narrow, one-lane and unpaved, and narrow en

From Twisp, take SR 20 east about 2 miles and continue south on SR 153 about 12 miles, then turn right onto Gold Creek Loop Road and follow it to Gold Creek Road. Drive Gold Creek Road about 5 miles, turn left onto Forest Road 4340-200, and follow it about 3.6 miles to the Foggy Dew Trailhead at road's end, about 3,400 ft. A Northwest Forest Pass or Interagency pass is required to park.

Three Fingers / Goat Flats Trailhead (Tupso Pass Rd)

text: From Granite Falls, drive the Mountain Loop Highway east to about milepost 7 and turn left (north) onto Forest Road 41, Tupso Pass Road. The road is closed to vehicles at the washed-out Canyon Creek bridge; park there and walk or bike the remaining 8 to 9 miles, staying on FR 41 past the side roads and then turning right onto FR 4160 to the trailhead at its end. There is no road in. Take the Lake Chelan ferry from Chelan or Field's Point to Lucerne, then the village shuttle up from the landing. Plan the whole trip around the boat and bus timetable in both directions — parties who miss the connection out spend an extra night at the village.

No road reaches this trailhead. Drive to Chelan or Field's Point Landing and take the Lady of the Lake ferry roughly four hours up the lake to Lucerne, then ride the Forest Service and Holden Village bus the remaining miles up to Holden Village at about 3,300 ft, where the Railroad Creek Trail begins. Check access before you commit to the ferry: FR 8301 between Lucerne and Holden, and Holden Villa

pins.name: Squire Creek Trailhead (Trail #654, end of FS Rd 2040)

text: From I-5 take the Arlington exit and follow SR 530 east through Oso to Darrington. From Highway 530 in town, go south on Madison Avenue to the T, turn right onto Darrington Street, and stay on it as it becomes Squire Creek Road. Drive to the washout that gates the road and park there. The road is badly washed out near its end from the 2002 Jumbo Mountain slide, and many parties now park about a th

From Twisp, take WA-20 east 2 miles to WA-153, then go south 12 miles to County Road 1029/1034, signed for Foggy Dew Campground. Follow that about 6 miles as it becomes FR 4340 — the pavement ends around mile 4, where you bear right — then continue on FR 4340-300 for roughly 4.6 more miles to the Crater Creek Trailhead at 4,750 ft. The lot has a vault toilet and stock facilities but no potable wat

From Twisp take SR 20 south two miles to the SR 153 junction, follow SR 153 south about twelve miles to County Road 1029 and on to CR 1034 (Gold Creek Road), which becomes FR 4340 after roughly five miles. Continue about 1.6 miles further, then turn onto FR 4340-300 (Crater Creek Road) and follow it about 4.6 miles to the trailhead at 4,750 ft; the gravel is washboarded in places, so drive it slow

From Darrington, take the Suiattle River Road (FR 26) east toward the trailhead. Check the current closure point before you go and build the extra road miles into the schedule — bikes are the usual answer to them. A day-use pass is required, and there is no potable water at the road end.

pins.name: Old Mine Road gate (parking for Niederprum Trail #653)

text: From Darrington, drive SR 530 west about 5 miles to the community of Whitehorse and turn left (south) onto 387th Ave NE, also called Old Mine Road, at the gas station and convenience store. Follow it 0.6 mile to its dead end at a steel gate and a barricade of large boulders, at about 540 ft, and park there. A free self-issued Boulder River Wilderness permit applies.

From SR 530 about 8 mi north of Darrington, turn east on the Suiattle River Road (FS Road 26) and follow it about 20 mi to the Downey Creek Trailhead at about 1,440 ft. Park on the south side of the road just past the Downey Creek bridge; the trail starts on the north side. A Northwest Forest Pass or day pass is required. The road has a long history of washouts, so check its status first.

Drive Libby Creek Road to its end at FS Road 4340-750, where the Libby Lake Trailhead — also called the Libby Creek Trailhead — sits at about 4,400 ft. Parking is roadside for roughly ten cars, with no facilities. No fee or pass is required here. Libby Creek Trail No. 415 starts from the road end and heads southwest into the Lake Chelan–Sawtooth Wilderness.

From Twisp, take SR 20 east about 3 miles to SR 153 and follow it south to Libby Creek Road (County Road 1045), about 1.4 miles south of Carlton. Follow Libby Creek Road about 2.5 miles, turn left onto FS Road 43 for about 5 miles, left onto FS Road 4340 for about 1.2 miles, right onto FS Road 4340-700 for 1.5 miles, then left onto FS Road 4340-750 to its end at about 4,430 ft. Roadside parking fo

From Twisp, follow the Twisp River Road west, turn up East Buttermilk Creek Road (FR-43), and take the FR-4300-500 spur to its end. Sign the wilderness register at the kiosk before starting up Trail #411.

There is no road into Stehekin. Drive to Fields Point Landing or Chelan and take the Lady of the Lake II or Lady Express up-lake — two to four hours depending on which boat — then ride the National Park Service shuttle up the Stehekin Valley Road to the Harlequin Bridge stop. There is no road to Stehekin. From Chelan, take the Lady of the Lake passenger ferry (or a floatplane) up Lake Chelan to Stehekin Landing, then ride the park shuttle bus about 4.4 miles up the Stehekin Valley Road to the Harlequin Bridge stop.

Park at the Eagle Creek/Oval trailhead at about 3,000 ft, at the end of FR 4420-080. Reach it on Twisp River Road/FR 44 roughly 12.5 miles west of Twisp, then turn up the West Buttermilk/FR 4420 spur and follow it to the road's end.
